title: A Method for SUMO Modification of Proteins in vitro
author: Christine C. Lee
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Gather materials and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all listed items with their catalog numbers: pipette tips (USA Scientific, 1111‑3700; 1111‑0700; 1112‑1720), X‑Ray film (RPI, 248300), Whatman Grade 2 filter paper (GE Healthcare, 1002‑917) cut to 10 × 9 cm, clear plastic wrap (Fisher Scientific, 22‑305654), 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes, recombinant SUMO1 or SUMO2, SUMO E1 (Aos/Uba2), SUMO E2, substrate plasmid (Addgene, 13379) or optional GST‑RanGAP1 (Enzo, BML‑UW9755‑0100), T N T® Quick Coupled Transcription/Translation System (Promega, L1170 or L2080), EasyTag L‑[³⁵S]‑Methionine (PerkinElmer, NEG709A005MC), ATP (Sigma‑Aldrich, A1852), phosphocreatine (Sigma‑Aldrich, P7936‑10MG), inorganic pyrophosphatase (Sigma‑Aldrich, I1643), HEPES (Fisher, BP310‑500), KOH pellets (Sigma‑Aldrich, 221473), potassium acetate (Sigma‑Aldrich, P1190), magnesium acetate tetrahydrate (Sigma‑Aldrich, M5661), DTT (Sigma‑Aldrich, 10197777001), acrylamide (Bio‑Rad, 1610101), 2 % Bis solution (Bio‑Rad, 1610142), APS (Bio‑Rad, 1610700), SDS (Sigma‑Aldrich, 436143), PageRuler protein ladder (Thermo Fisher, 26619), glycerol (Sigma‑Aldrich, G5516), bromophenol blue (Sigma‑Aldrich, B0126), β‑mercaptoethanol (Sigma‑Aldrich, M3148), Trizma® base (Sigma‑Aldrich, T1503), HCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, H1758), creatine phosphokinase (Sigma‑Aldrich, C3755), methanol (Fisher, A412‑4), glacial acetic acid (Fisher, A38‑212), glycine (Sigma‑Aldrich, G7126‑5KG), plus the recipes for SDS sample buffer, SUMO master mix, 12.5 % SDS‑PAGE gels and destaining solution.

steps.title: Handle radioactive materials safely
steps.instruction: Ensure all personnel are trained for ³⁵S‑methionine work, designate a dedicated containment area, and dispose of all tips, tubes and reagents as radioactive waste according to institutional guidelines.

steps.title: Prepare SUMO enzymes from E. coli
steps.instruction: Express and purify recombinant SUMO1/2, SUMO E1 (Aos/Uba2) and SUMO E2 enzymes in E. coli as described in Yang et al., 2018. Store the purified enzymes at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: In‑vitro transcription/translation of substrate
steps.instruction: Thaw a tube of rabbit reticulocyte lysate (Promega) on ice. For each substrate, add 20 µl lysate to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube on ice, return the remainder to –80 °C (avoid repeat freeze‑thaw). Add 2 µl ³⁵S‑methionine, keep on ice. Add 500 ng plasmid DNA encoding the substrate, keep on ice. Incubate the mixture in a 30 °C water bath for 60–90 min.

steps.title: Prepare SDS sample buffer (2×)
steps.instruction: Mix the following to make 2× SDS sample buffer and store aliquots at room temperature (stock solutions at –20 °C): 0.313 M Tris‑HCl pH 6.8, 4 % SDS, 20 % glycerol, 3.5 M β‑mercaptoethanol, 0.1 % (w/v) bromophenol blue.

steps.title: Prepare SUMO master mix
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube combine ultrapure water with: 20 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.3, 110 mM potassium acetate, 2 mM magnesium acetate, 200 nM SUMO E1, 600 nM SUMO E2, 1 µM SUMO1 or SUMO2, 20 U ml⁻¹ creatine phosphokinase, 5 mM phosphocreatine, 0.6 U ml⁻¹ inorganic pyrophosphatase, 1 mM DTT, and finally add 1 mM ATP last. Keep the mix on ice; each reaction will receive 28 µl of this master mix.

steps.title: Prepare 12.5 % SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Prepare stacking gel: 30 % acrylamide (final 0.44 % Bis‑acrylamide) in 0.5 M Tris‑HCl pH 6.8. Prepare resolving gel: 33.5 % acrylamide (final 0.3 % Bis‑acrylamide) in 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 9.1. Add 3 % ammonium persulfate (APS) freshly prepared in ultrapure water and TEMED as polymerization catalyst. Store gels at 4 °C protected from light. Prepare 1× running buffer by diluting a 4× stock (250 ml stock + 750 ml ultrapure water) to give 0.025 M Tris‑HCl, 0.192 M glycine, 0.1 % SDS.

steps.title: Prepare destaining solution
steps.instruction: Make a solution of 20 % (v/v) methanol and 10 % (v/v) glacial acetic acid in distilled/deionized water. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: In‑vitro SUMO modification
steps.instruction: Place 28 µl of freshly prepared SUMO master mix in a 1.5 ml tube at room temperature. Add 2 µl of the transcription/translation product, gently pipette up‑and‑down several times to mix (total volume 30 µl). Incubate the reaction in a 30 °C water bath (duration as required by experiment). Add 20 µl 2× SDS sample buffer to stop the reaction. Heat the mixture at 95 °C for 5 min. Briefly centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 30–60 sec at room temperature.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load 10 µl of each stopped reaction into wells of the 12.5 % gel, reserving lane 1 for 2 µl protein ladder. Run the gel at 70 V, room temperature, for ~20 min until the dye front reaches just below the stacking gel. Then increase to 120 V, room temperature, and run for an additional 2 h, stopping before the 10 kDa marker reaches the bottom (or when the dye front reaches the bottom). Disassemble the gel apparatus, slide a surgical blade between glass plates to release the gel, and discard the stacking gel. Transfer the running gel to a dish containing destaining solution and gently shake for 10 min at room temperature. Discard the used destaining solution into a radiation‑waste container. Add MilliQ water, shake 10 min at room temperature, and repeat the water wash at least three times.

steps.title: Perform autoradiography
steps.instruction: On a clean benchtop designated as a radiation area, lay a piece of Whatman™ Grade 2 paper. Place the washed gel onto the paper with lane 1 (protein ladder) oriented correctly. Overlay the gel with a piece of clear plastic wrap. Position the assembly on a gel dryer (paper directly on the foam, plastic wrap on top) and dry for ~30 min. Remove the plastic wrap and let the gel sit for 5 min on the benchtop. In a dark room, place the dried gel (still on the Whatman paper) inside an X‑ray cassette, lay an X‑ray film sheet on top, close the cassette, and keep it in darkness overnight at room temperature. Develop the film according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
